Plus, prayers to anyone who had to find a last-minute hotel room during last week’s flying nightmare. Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. items.title: Japan’s most powerful supercomputer may have been hacked, over 4,000 users’ personal data stolen
items.summary: Fugaku, Japan's most powerful supercomputer, has suffered a suspected data breach, with the information of more than 4,000 of its users potentially stolen as a result.

items.title: Banning phones really does help kids learn, researchers say
items.summary: A new nationwide study found that in-school cellphone bans can lead to modest improvements in learning. Now, researchers want to understand whether kids' phone use outside the classroom might contribute to the rest of students' learning loss - using the conditions of Meta's multibillion-dollar settlement from earlier this year. items.title: AMD grabs over 40% of new TOP500 list for supercomputers, up 14% since last year — new Lux system developed between AMD and Department of Energy debuts at no. 14 with EPYC CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPUs
items.summary: AMD's Lux supercomputer debuted at position 14 on the new TOP500 list published during SC26. It's one of two machines AMD is developing as part of a $1 billion deal with the U.S. Department of Energy.
